name: synthetic_mast_testbed_v7_method_error
author: first_agent
entrant_go: 2026-10-01 (pasted step 2: synthetic Thomson, run v7, measure D_LCFS and Consistency with an exact machine model)
question: What error does our v7 MAST solver make when the machine model is exact, i.e. on synthetic MAST equilibria from our own FreeGS generator with synthetic inputs?
rule_3: MAST inputs only for the generator (step 1c) and the synthetic inputs; no MAST equilibrium field, demo shot or leaderboard number selects anything. The public v7 MAST components (flux .9805, D .1884, Cons .2732, observed) are quoted beside the result for description only; nothing is chosen by them.
truth: step 1c arm s0.5 maps (step1c_maps.npz), frames passing an inclusion filter written after step 1c was seen (disclosed; it selects testbed frames, not a MAST component): converged, Ip within 1 %, Reader contour, axis R .5-1.2 and |Z| <= .3, inboard crossing <= r_in + .01 and >= .12, outboard crossing >= r_out - .01 and <= r_out + .20, control change <= 10 % of P4+P5.
synthetic_inputs: coil currents = the real frame's per-filament ampere-turns plus each control circuit's FreeGS change spread equally over its filaments; Ip and TF current as the real frame; Thomson on the real shot's channels: psiN from the truth map (Reader axis and LCFS levels), Te = Te0 (1 - psiN^2)^1.5 inside, Te0 0.02 exp(-(psiN-1)/0.03) outside, Te0 = the real frame's smoothed Thomson peak; ne = 3e19 (1 - 0.8 psiN^2) inside, 0.6e19 outside. One fixed profile, no search.
solver_under_test: v7 entrypoint copy (../../v8/entrypoints_v7_copy, thomson_isoflux.reconstruct) on a one-frame Shot built from the synthetic inputs.
metrics: as reeval/r2_stage_attribution.score_shot with Reader('MAST'): per frame D = symmetric Hausdorff / R_geo of the truth contour, the 7 consistency scalars, flux sse; pooled flux R2, mean D, Consistency = mean over the 7 of max(0, R2) across frames; solved count.
decision_rule: none: a measurement. Interpretation fixed in advance: synthetic D and Consistency close to the observed public v7 values -> the MAST loss is mostly method error (improvable on this testbed); much better on synthetic -> the loss is mostly model error (machine, passive currents, profiles, solenoid share), which the testbed cannot fix.
